recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the current-build seed issue without undoing the later FM decision to prefer, rather than require extensible, bindings in the base specification.
issue_request: FHIR-17954 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FM issue for STU3 CERq/EligibilityRequest asking to change .priority binding strength to extensible, with resolution also applying the priority-code binding change across other financial resources.
initial_application: The 2018 GF#17954 batch commit f369c813fb touched the old coverage eligibility request spreadsheet but left the ProcessPriority conformance as example; the 2021 source rework 33b409a4b6 converted that content into the active CoverageEligibilityRequest StructureDefinition and preserved the example strength.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini makes CoverageEligibilityRequest the active current-build successor to EligibilityRequest. Later R6 FM issues changed the same ProcessPriority binding on Claim and ExplanationOfBenefit from example to extensible (FHIR-49886) and then to preferred under FHIR-53057's broader policy that base FM bindings should not exceed preferred.
reconciliation: Changed source/coverageeligibilityrequest/structuredefinition-CoverageEligibilityRequest.xml so CoverageEligibilityRequest.priority uses preferred binding strength for http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/process-priority. Retired EligibilityRequest spreadsheet content and generated-looking SVG artifacts were left unchanged.
